newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican pension funds restricted from equity-gov't.
newsitem.headline: Mexican pension funds restricted from equity-gov't.

text.p: Mexico's new private pension funds will be restricted from investing in the country's stock market for their first year of operations, officials said on Wednesday.

"They will not be allowed to invest in stocks. In the rules, they are limited to investing in debt instruments," Salvador Alonso, vice-president of planning at the National Retirement Savings Association (Consar), told Reuters.
Consar published rules governing the new pesion system, which started officially on Monday, last weekend but it did not specify the funds would be banned from equity investment. The funds
will be allowed to invest up to 35 percent of their portfolios in private debt instruments, according to the rules.
The rules are aimed at ensuring workers' investment will not erode in real terms to inflation. Funds must invest at least 51 percent in inflation-indexed instruments known as UDIs.
"By law, these are limited for now to investing in instruments which preserve the workers' purchasing power," Alonso said.

However, Alonso said the government plans to allow each pension fund company to begin offering workers the choice of investing in riskier funds sometime next year, including funds which can buy equity.
